claims: The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is a Cabinet-level federal agency.

The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) provides healthcare, disability compensation, education assistance, home loans, and burial benefits to eligible military veterans and their families.
The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) was established in 1988.
The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) operates medical centers, clinics, and national cemeteries nationwide.
The VA is structured into three primary administrations.
Veterans Health Administration (VHA) operates 170 medical centers.
Veterans Health Administration (VHA) operates numerous outpatient clinics.
Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) manages disability compensation.
Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) manages pension.
Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) manages education/training (GI Bill).
Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) manages vocational rehabilitation.
National Cemetery Administration (NCA) provides burial and memorial benefits to eligible veterans and family members at 135 national cemeteries.
VA eligibility generally requires active military service.
VA eligibility generally requires a discharge that is not dishonorable.
VA offers home loan guarantees.
VA offers life insurance.
VA offers specialized services for disabled veterans.
The VA main hotline is 800-698-2411.
VA.gov has a facility locator.
Ask VA (AVA) is an online tool to find answers and submit questions.
National Personnel Records Center is for requesting military service records.
National Personnel Records Center is for replacing medals.
VA News provides updates on technology and services.
